comment: Hand-computed scratch certificate wire v1 vectors (lane V). No production encoder or decoder produced any byte here. Each 'layout' lists the bytes of docs/design/scratch-facts.md in wire order: version 01, then S,F,E,H,J, each set as a complete byte (00/01), an unsigned 64-bit little-endian count, then per entry an unsigned 64-bit little-endian length followed by raw bytes. 'certificate' is the concatenation of its layout blocks, retyped independently; tests assert the equality.

vectors.name: doc_worked_vector
vectors.note: The worked vector of docs/design/scratch-facts.md, 82 bytes: S={ab} F={one empty string} E={x} H={} J={q}, every set complete. 1 + (1+8+8+2) + (1+8+8+0) + (1+8+8+1) + (1+8) + (1+8+8+1) = 82.

vectors.name: incomplete_exit_out_of_subset
vectors.note: E is a dynamic exit-ID set (complete=00). S={L} F={empty string} H={empty,L} J={L}. 1 + 18 + 17 + 18 + (1+8+8+8+1) + 18 = 98 bytes. An out_of_subset label is accepted over any certificate.

vectors.name: sorted_multi_entry_and_nul_byte
vectors.note: S={B,a} in unsigned-byte order (0x42 before 0x61), E={a NUL b} proves NUL is an ordinary byte, F and H are empty, J={B,a}. 1 + (1+8+16+2) + 9 + (1+8+8+3) + 9 + (1+8+16+2) = 93 bytes.
